text:
Sam H: heads-up — after deploy 12f8e9 we saw ~15% tail latency regression on small-batch (<8) inference. grabbed an nsys trace and a perfetto timeline. wondering if kernel selection changed.
Anja L: thanks — can you paste the nsys top kernel time breakdown? quick numbers are fine.
Sam H: here's the top kernels (nsys summary):
```
Top kernels by total time:
1) kv_prefetch_v4         42.3%  (18.2s)
2) attn_fwd_qkv_fused     28.7%  (12.3s)
3) batch_dispatcher      12.9%  (5.5s)
4) compact_kv_pack         6.1%  (2.6s)
5) softmax_reduce         4.0%  (1.7s)
6) memcopy_h2d            3.5%  (1.5s)
```
The trace shows kv_prefetch_v4 spiking on many small sequences.
Devon R: hmm kv_prefetch_v4 is new variant from PR #4397 (changed prefetch stride + async launch). possible regressed scheduling. what does SM occupancy look like?
Sam H: occupancy and warp efficiency from nsight sampler: kv_prefetch_v4 occupancy low (~18%) and high warp stall on memory dependency. attn_fwd has good occupancy but longer runtime per thread.
Anja L: so prefetch kernel is grabbing a lot of wall time but not using SMs well — could be serializing on global mem. any kv cache hits changed?
Sam H: cache hit rate dropped ~6% for these traces (seen in our app-level counters). Also saw increased number of kernel launches per request: from ~6 to ~18 for small batches.
perf-ci: automated-trace: regression signature matched pattern "nv_kv_prefetch_explode" across 6/6 CI runs. commit 12f8e9 touches kernel launch batching logic.
Devon R: can you post the exact nsys command you used? i'll run locally and attach perfetto.
Sam H: nsys profile --sample=none --stats=true -o /tmp/trace ./bin/infer --model redwood-open-13b --batch 4 --seq-len 64
Perfetto: used --dump=timeline.pb and opened in UI — notable kernel fan-out at request boundaries.
Anja L: hypothesis: batching heuristic now splits micro-batches into more kernel launches to service prefetch latency; overhead dominates for small batches. solution options:
- revert to older prefetch stride in kv_prefetch_v3 (cheap)
- coalesce prefetches across requests in batch_dispatcher (medium risk)
- increase BATCH_WINDOW_US for small-batch paths (low-risk)
Devon R: quick test: set env BATCH_WINDOW_US=200 and rerun nsys. if kernel count drops and kv_prefetch_v4 time drops, we confirm batching fragmentation cause.
Sam H: running that now. ETA ~8m.
(perf-ci reacts with :white_check_mark:)
Sam H: update — with BATCH_WINDOW_US=200 total kernel launches down from 18->7, kv_prefetch_v4 time drops to 15% total. tail latency back to baseline in my run.
Anja L: OK good signal. next steps: create a small PR to gate the new stride behind a flag and add a unit trace test that asserts kernel launches <= 10 for batch<=8. assign to Devon.
Devon R: will do. i'll also add an nsight script to auto-flag low-occupancy kernels (occupancy <25% && time share>20%).
infra-bot: scheduled nightly trace run queued (job id: 8743). will run across gpu-pool-a and gpu-pool-b and report if regression persists.
Sam H: thanks all — filing followups: PR draft, perf test, and a quick rollback plan if CI flags persist. :thumbsup:
Anja L: capturing this in the perf board. tagging ops to watch deploy window tomorrow.
Devon R: linking logs and the nsys zip to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1259
Sam H: end.
